study_identification_part.si_4_title: Atypical maturation of the functional connectome hierarchy in autism

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the generalized additive model for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS) with a four-parameter sinh-arcsinh (SHASH) distribution to model nonlinear age-related patterns of cortical hierarchy. P-splines were used as the nonlinear function for age effects. The GAMLSS model fitted parameters for mean (μ), variance (σ), skewness (ν), and kurtosis (τ) of the feature distribution.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Normative models were constructed using the GAMLSS model [24, 39], which allowed us to capture nonlinear age-related patterns of cortical hierarchy in TD individuals and identify deviations in ASD relative to this normative pattern. ... Fitting the GAMLSS model involves a four-parameter distribution modeling µ, σ, ν, and τ; corresponding to the mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis of the feature distribution, respectively. We used the four-parameter sinh-arcsinh (SHASH) distribution [42], following the recommendations for the normative modeling of neuroimaging data [43].

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The primary response variable was the principal functional connectivity gradient (G1) representing the sensory-DMN axis of cortical hierarchy. Gradients were estimated from resting-state fMRI data using diffusion map embedding applied to functional connectivity matrices computed from the Schaefer 200-parcel atlas. The study also examined the second gradient (G2) representing the sensorimotor-visual axis as a secondary analysis.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The principal functional connectivity gradient representing cortical hierarchy was estimated using diffusion map embedding. ... We estimated cortex-wide functional connectivity gradients from preprocessed BOLD data using the Schaefer atlas [31] with 200 parcels. ... Low-dimensional representations, referred to as gradients, were extracted from this matrix by using diffusion map embedding [35] for each participant.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.answer: Age-related: Age; Demographics: Sex; Interactions: Age×Sex
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included age (modeled with P-spline nonlinear function), sex, and the interaction between age and sex as explanatory variables. The model equation was specified as: Gradient ~ f(age) + sex + f(age) * sex, where f(x) is a P-spline nonlinear function. Site effects in the ABIDE dataset were addressed through ComBat harmonization applied to the gradient values prior to modeling.
